condition.rationale: Exterior photos show straight, glossy paint, an intact front fascia, stock ride height and no visible fault lamps. Minor scratches are disclosed. No underbody, engine-bay, interior or tire-date evidence, and no service invoices. Condition is unproven either way at 175k miles.

price_value.rationale: $20,000 sits near the top of the $13,619–$21,411 fair-value band, about 23% over the $16,301 mid. A comparable 2017 Premium at 165,800 miles sold for $17,750, and a 173k 2017 Premium peer asks $21,000. The included platform rack adds modest value, but there are no records to support a premium.

mission_fit.rationale: Directly serves the capability intent: body-on-frame 4WD, low range, already set up with a platform rack, and the rooftop tent is available for $1,000. seller_questions: What is the VIN, and which trim is it (Base, Premium or Luxury)? Does it have KDSS?
Can you send invoices or a dealer service printout showing spark plugs, coolant, transmission and transfer-case/differential fluid changes, with dates and mileages?
Has the check-engine light ever shown P2440, P2442 or other secondary air injection codes, and has the air pump or switching valves been replaced? Receipt?
Will you allow an independent pre-purchase inspection at a Lexus/Toyota shop near Farmington before any deposit?
Can you send photos of the frame rails, rear crossmember, hitch area and underside of the engine (valley/timing cover area)?
What has the hitch been used for? What was the heaviest load towed, and how often?
What brand are the tires, and what are the four-digit DOT date codes?
Which rack is fitted, how is it mounted (factory points or drilled), and are there any roof leaks or seal issues?
When did you buy it, from whom (Superior Automotive?), and was it bought new or used?
Can you send a cold-start video from fully cold, including the first 60 seconds of idle?
Has it been in any accident or had paint/bodywork, even minor?
ppi_focus: Full OBD scan including stored, pending and permanent codes and readiness monitors, focusing on secondary air injection (P2440/P2442/P2445) and the air pump/valves
KDSS: confirm fitment; inspect cylinders, lines and accumulator for leaks; check for lean at rest
Rear of the block and timing cover for coolant/oil seepage (valley plate leak); coolant level and condition
Frame rails, rear crossmember, hitch mounting area and rocker pinch welds for rust, rust repair or towing stress
Transmission, transfer case and differential fluid condition; test 4WD high/low, center diff lock and transfer actuator
Suspension bushings, ball joints, shocks and steering rack for 175k-mile wear; front brake rotors and calipers
Roof: rack mount points, drill holes, sealant and headliner water staining from rack/tent use
Tire date codes, tread depth and even wear (alignment)
Paint meter on panels to check for undisclosed bodywork
what_would_change_verdict: A VIN plus a clean history report and dealer service records covering plugs, fluids and coolant would raise documentation substantially.
A clean independent PPI, with no air-injection codes, no KDSS or valley-plate leaks and a rust-free frame, would move condition up.
A price nearer the $16–17k fair-value mid, or the tent included at the same price, would improve value.
Down: refusal of VIN or PPI, stored P2440/P2442 codes, KDSS leaks, frame rust or heavy towing history.
evidence.mission_note: This fits the capability branch genuinely: a body-on-frame 4WD already carrying a roof platform, with a rooftop tent available, gives the camping capability the RX 350 lacks. It still needs records and a PPI to justify the 175k miles and an above-mid asking price.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2017 GX460 at 174,994 miles (odometer photographed), brown over tan, with a stated clean title. It has an aftermarket platform roof rack and receiver hitch, and the OVS rooftop tent is optionally available for $1,000. Photos show a straight, stock-height body on factory wheels and no fault lamps in a single idling dash shot. Nothing observed is wrong beyond the disclosed minor scratches. Everything model-critical remains open: no VIN, trim or KDSS fitment; no secondary air injection history; no underbody or frame photos; no records beyond an oil-change claim. The $20,000 asking price sits near the top of the $13,619–$21,411 fair-value band, against a $17,750 sale for a comparable 2017 Premium at 165,800 miles. The hitch and overland setup raise questions about towing and trail use that only an inspection and records can answer.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, trim and any service records, and ask whether an independent PPI near Farmington can be done before any deposit.
